dedupe_keys.name: a national dataset of annual urban extent 1985 2015 in the conterminous united states using landsat time series data

description: The US urban-extent research team publishes annual urban expansion across the conterminous United States for 1985–2015. Landsat-derived grids record urbanisation at 30 m resolution and are packaged into 49 state-level units. GeoTIFFs use an Albers Equal Area Conic projection. A year-code lookup table, state-name spreadsheet and legend explain how pixel values represent urbanisation dates. Figshare distributes the ZIP package and supporting tables publicly and free under CC-BY-4.0. A limitation is that mapped urban extent is a land-cover classification, not an inventory of buildings, residents or infrastructure capacity. Classification and date uncertainty require attention when using individual pixels. The time series could support urban-growth simulation calibration or reconstruction of changing flood exposure. It complements population grids with an independent spatial history of developed land. The record preserves the repository’s stated packaging count without assuming that it includes additional US territories.
